blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment through the client-supplied name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: An agent allowed to read one ticket of their team passes the authorization check at line 28, then sends name="../43/contract.pdf" to read another team's attachment, name="../../../../etc/passwd" or an absolute path such as "/etc/passwd" (which makes os.path.join discard the base) to read any file the service can open (CWE-22). Do not open a path built from the request: look the name up in the attachments table for that ticket_id (the row save_attachment inserts) and refuse it when absent, and additionally reject any name that differs from os.path.basename(name) or whose resolved real path is not under os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id)).
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment through the client-supplied name

findings.evidence:
def save_attachment(ticket_id: int, filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:
    """Stores an uploaded file under the ticket's directory; returns its name."""
    name = os.path.basename(filename)
    directory = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))
findings.recommendation: The proposal says agents upload files to a ticket, yet the upload takes no agent_id and never calls may_read_ticket, unlike read_attachment; if the agent's ticket_id reaches it unchecked, an agent writes (and, with the same filename, overwrites) attachments of another team's ticket. The caller is not in the change, so this could not be confirmed. Take the agent_id and enforce the same ownership check as read_attachment before writing.
findings.title: save_attachment stores into any ticket without an authorization check
